table.name: account
table.purpose: Czech market/trade fee records: one row per fee assessment, linking a district (okres) to a fee type and a due date. Referenced by many other tables, so it is the central entity (likely a fee/lease case).

col_001.name: fee_id
col_001.description: Primary key, surrogate integer identifier for the fee record; referenced by many other tables.

col_002.name: district_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to the district lookup (t05), values 1-77 matching Czech okres codes (e.g. 35 Jablonec n. Nisou, 77 Vsetin).

col_003.name: fee_type
col_003.description: Fee charging frequency in Czech: 'POPLATEK MESICNE' = monthly fee, 'POPLATEK TYDNE' = weekly fee, 'POPLATEK PO OBRATU' = fee per turnover.

col_004.name: due_date
col_004.description: Date of the fee record, ranging 2049-01-01 to 2053-12-29. The far-future years are likely a shifted/anonymized or mis-parsed date; the exact real-world meaning (due date vs. assessment date) is unresolved.

table.name: card
table.purpose: One row per customer/member account: an internal surrogate ID, an external person ID, a membership tier, and a membership expiry (or similar) date. Referenced by many other tables, so it is the central entity of the database. The future-dated dates (2049–2054) suggest synthetic or shifted data; the exact date semantics are uncertain.

col_001.name: customer_id
col_001.description: Primary key of t02; unique surrogate identifier for each customer/member row. Referenced by t01, t03, t05, and t06 as a foreign key.

col_002.name: person_id
col_002.description: Unique external identifier linking each customer to a person record in t04 and t03 (one-to-one). Could be a person/customer number from another system; the exact meaning of the number is unresolved.

col_003.name: membership_tier
col_003.description: Customer membership tier with three levels: classic (659), junior (145), gold (88). 'junior' suggests an age-based or entry-level category; exact tier semantics beyond the labels are unknown.

col_004.name: membership_expiry_date
col_004.description: A future date per customer (2049-11-07 to 2054-12-29). Plausibly a membership expiry or renewal date; alternatively a contract end or subscription end date. The far-future range may indicate synthetic or offset data.

table.name: client
table.purpose: Person-level registry (likely patients or citizens): one row per person with an ID, sex, birth date, and district of residence (Czech districts per the lookup labels). Referenced by many other tables as the person key.

col_001.name: person_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique person identifier. Referenced one-to-one by t04 and many-to-one by t01, t05, t06, t07, t02, so it is the central entity key of the database.

col_002.name: sex
col_002.description: Sex of the person: M = male, F = female.

col_003.name: birth_date
col_003.description: Date of birth of the person. Range 1967–2043 with future dates present, so some values are synthetic/erroneous; the wide spread and near-uniqueness fit birth dates rather than event dates.

col_004.name: district_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to district lookup t05.col_001 (Czech districts, e.g. 35 = Jablonec n. Nisou, 77 = Vsetin); the person's district, most likely of residence.

table.name: disposition
table.purpose: Links clients to accounts and states their role on the account (owner or authorized user/disponent). One row per client-account relationship. This matches the 'disp' table of the Czech Berka financial dataset: 5369 rows, 4500 OWNER and 869 DISPONENT entries, with each client owning exactly one account (one-to-one with the client table) and accounts possibly having additional authorized users.

col_001.name: disposition_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the disposition (client-account relationship) record. Unique across all 5369 rows. Referenced by rows in t05, t06, t02, t07, t08 (e.g. loans, cards, transactions linked to a disposition).

col_002.name: client_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the client participating in this disposition. Unique here (each client appears exactly once), matching a one-to-one join to the client table t03. In the sample rows it equals col_001, but its range (max 13998 vs 13690) shows it is a distinct identifier sequence.

col_003.name: account_id
col_003.description: Identifier of the account the client is attached to. Foreign key to the account table (t01, many dispositions to one account). 4500 distinct accounts; the 4500 OWNER rows map one-to-one to accounts, while the 869 DISPONENT rows attach additional authorized users to existing accounts.

col_004.name: disposition_type
col_004.description: Role of the client on the account: 'OWNER' (account holder, 4500 rows) or 'DISPONENT' (authorized user/disponent who may operate the account, 869 rows).

table.name: district
table.purpose: Demographic and economic profile of Czech districts (okresy); one row per district. Matches the 'district' table of the classic Czech bank/financial dataset (77 Czech districts).

col_002.name: district_name
col_002.description: Name of the district (e.g. Benesov, Brno - mesto, Jablonec n. Nisou).

col_003.name: region
col_003.description: Region of the Czech Republic the district belongs to (8 values: Prague, central/north/south/east/west Bohemia, north/south Moravia).

col_004.name: inhabitants
col_004.description: Number of inhabitants of the district (min ~42.8k, max ~1.2M for Prague).

col_005.name: municipalities_under_500
col_005.description: Number of municipalities with fewer than 500 inhabitants.

col_008.name: municipalities_over_10000
col_008.description: Number of municipalities with more than 10000 inhabitants (small counts 0-5).

col_009.name: number_of_cities
col_009.description: Number of cities in the district (1-11).

col_011.name: average_salary
col_011.description: Average yearly salary in the district (CZK, ~8110-12541).

col_013.name: unemployment_rate_1996
col_013.description: Unemployment rate in 1996 (percent, 0.43-9.4); slightly higher than col_012, consistent with year-over-year rates.

col_015.name: committed_crimes_1995
col_015.description: Number of committed crimes in 1995 (818-85677, Prague being the outlier).

col_016.name: committed_crimes_1996
col_016.description: Number of committed crimes in 1996 (888-99107); slightly higher than col_015, consistent with year-over-year counts.

table.purpose: Each row appears to be a transaction/order record (one-to-one with a record in t01) carrying a date, a duration in months (12/24/36/48/60), an amount, a monetary value, and a category code. The exact business domain is not determinable from the data alone.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of the table; unique integer identifier for each row.

col_002.name: t01_id
col_002.description: References t01.col_001 one-to-one; a unique identifier linking each row to exactly one record in t01 (e.g. a parent transaction or account).

col_003.name: date
col_003.description: A date between 2049 and 2054, likely the record's transaction/effective date. The future-dated values suggest synthetic or offset data; the exact semantic (issue, maturity, due date) is unresolved.

col_005.name: term_months
col_005.description: One of 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 — evenly distributed. Almost certainly a term/duration in months (1–5 years), e.g. loan or contract term. Also joins to small lookup tables t02/t03/t04, which may hold term labels.

col_007.name: category_code
col_007.description: Four-level code A/B/C/D with C most common (~59%), A (~30%), D and B rare. A category/tier/rating code; the meaning of each letter is not determinable from the data.

table.name: order
table.purpose: Financial transactions table (Czech PKDD-style data): each row is one transaction on an account, with an amount, a transaction category (SIPO household payments, UVER loan, POJISTNE insurance, LEASING), and a reference to an account/client entity in t01/t03/t04.

col_001.name: transaction_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique sequential transaction identifier.

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Reference to the account (or client) the transaction belongs to; many-to-one join to t01.col_001 (also accepted by t03/t04 primary keys). Values 1-11362.

col_004.name: partner_account_number
col_004.description: Nearly unique 8-digit number (399-99994199), likely the counterparty (partner) account number for the transaction. Alternative reading: a bank/account identifier; evidence favors counterparty account since it is almost unique per row.

col_005.name: amount
col_005.description: Transaction amount in the local currency (CZK), range 1-14882, median ~2596.

col_006.name: transaction_category
col_006.description: Transaction characterization: SIPO (household/utility payments), UVER (loan payment), POJISTNE (insurance), LEASING (leasing payment), or empty (uncategorized/other). Czech labels from PKDD financial dataset.

table.name: trans
table.purpose: Bank account transactions (per-account ledger): each row is one transaction on an account, with amount, resulting balance, type, operation, and characterization codes. Matches the structure of the PKDD'99 Czech bank 'trans' table (Czech labels: VYDAJ=expense, PRIJEM=income, VYBER=withdrawal).

col_001.name: transaction_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique sequential transaction identifier (1..3,682,987 across the dataset, 1,056,320 rows here).

col_002.name: account_id
col_002.description: Owning account identifier; references t01.col_001 (accounts table), many transactions per account (4,500 distinct accounts).

col_003.name: transaction_date
col_003.description: Date of the transaction (stored as string), spanning 2049-01-01 to 2054-12-31 (dates shifted from the original 1993-1998 data).

col_004.name: type
col_004.description: Transaction type in Czech: PRIJEM = income/credit, VYDAJ = expense/debit, VYBER = cash withdrawal.

col_005.name: operation
col_005.description: Operation mode (Czech): VYBER = cash withdrawal, VKLAD = cash deposit, PREVOD NA UCET = transfer to another account, PREVOD Z UCTU = transfer from another account, VYBER KARTOU = card withdrawal. Null (17.3%) where no operation applies.

col_006.name: amount
col_006.description: Transaction amount in the account currency (CZK); min 0, max 87,400, median 2,100.

col_007.name: balance
col_007.description: Account balance after the transaction (CZK); can be negative (min -41,126), max 209,637.

col_008.name: k_symbol
col_008.description: Transaction characterization (Czech): UROK = interest credited, SLUZBY = services/payment for statement, SIPO = household/utility payments, DUCHOD = old-age pension, SANKC. UROK = sanction interest, POJISTNE = insurance payment, UVER = loan payment. Blank/null when not applicable (45.6%).

col_009.name: bank
col_009.description: Code of the counterparty bank for inter-bank transfers (two-letter codes); null (74.1%) for non-transfer transactions.

col_010.name: account
col_010.description: Counterparty account number for inter-bank transfers; 0 and nulls common (72% null) when no counterparty applies. Values up to 99,994,199 look like account numbers, not a foreign key to this database.
